title: Pharmacology Midterm Review
description: A comprehensive 25-item pharmacology quiz covering drug calculations, mechanisms of action, pharmacokinetics, and clinical situational analysis

questions.questionText: A physician orders Amoxicillin 500 mg PO every 8 hours. The pharmacy stocks 250 mg/5 mL suspension. Using the formula $$\text{Volume} = \frac{\text{Desired Dose}}{\text{Dose on Hand}} \times \text{Volume on Hand}$$ how many mL should be administered per dose?

A nurse is caring for a 68-year-old male with hypertension who is newly prescribed Lisinopril 10 mg daily. On day 3, the patient calls the clinic reporting a persistent dry cough. What is the most appropriate nursing action?

options.text: Instruct the patient to stop the medication immediately and visit the ER
Document the symptom and notify the physician, as this is a known side effect of ACE inhibitors
Reassure the patient that the cough will resolve on its own without intervention
Advise the patient to double the dose to build tolerance

questions.questionText: Beta-blockers work by blocking beta-adrenergic receptors, thereby decreasing heart rate and blood pressure.

Using the Cockcroft-Gault equation for Creatinine Clearance: $$CrCl = \frac{(140 - \text{Age}) \times \text{Weight (kg)}}{72 \times \text{Serum Creatinine (mg/dL)}}$$ Calculate the CrCl for a 70-year-old male weighing 70 kg with a serum creatinine of 1.0 mg/dL.
Review the drug comparison table below. Which drug class is associated with hyperkalemia as a side effect?
The therapeutic index is calculated as: $$TI = \frac{TD_{50}}{ED_{50}}$$ A drug with a narrow therapeutic index requires more careful monitoring because the toxic dose is close to the effective dose.

A patient weighing 60 kg is prescribed Gentamicin at 5 mg/kg/day divided every 8 hours. The available concentration is 40 mg/2 mL. How many mL will the nurse administer per dose? $$\text{Dose per administration} = \frac{5 \times 60}{3}$$
A 55-year-old woman with Type 2 Diabetes is admitted for a scheduled CT scan with contrast. She takes Metformin 1000 mg twice daily. What is the most appropriate action prior to the procedure?

options.text: Hold Metformin 48 hours before and after the contrast procedure to prevent lactic acidosis
Double the Metformin dose to compensate for contrast-induced changes
Administer Metformin as usual — no interaction with contrast dye exists
Switch immediately to insulin before the procedure

questions.questionText: First-pass metabolism refers to the phenomenon where a drug is metabolized in the liver before reaching systemic circulation, reducing its bioavailability.
Based on the pharmacokinetics table below, which drug has the longest half-life?

Half-life is the time required for the plasma concentration of a drug to decrease by half. Using $$t_{1/2} = \frac{0.693}{k_e}$$ where $k_e$ is the elimination rate constant, a drug with $k_e = 0.0693 \text{ hr}^{-1}$ has a half-life of _____ hours.
A 45-year-old male patient on Warfarin therapy presents with an INR of 5.8 (target range: 2.0–3.0). He has no active bleeding. What is the most appropriate management?

options.text: Hold Warfarin, administer Vitamin K orally, and recheck INR in 24–48 hours
Continue Warfarin at the same dose and recheck INR next week
Double the Warfarin dose to recalibrate the INR

questions.questionText: Morphine and other opioids exert their analgesic effect primarily by binding to $\mu$-opioid receptors in the central nervous system.

An IV infusion of Dopamine is ordered at 5 mcg/kg/min for a patient weighing 80 kg. The solution available is Dopamine 400 mg in 250 mL D5W. Using: $$\text{Rate (mL/hr)} = \frac{\text{Dose (mcg/kg/min)} \times \text{Weight (kg)} \times 60}{\text{Concentration (mcg/mL)}}$$ what is the infusion rate in mL/hr?
Review the antibiotic spectrum table. Which antibiotic is most appropriate for a confirmed MRSA infection?
A 30-year-old pregnant woman (28 weeks) is prescribed an antibiotic for a UTI. Which of the following is the SAFEST choice during pregnancy?

Volume of distribution ($V_d$) is calculated as: $$V_d = \frac{\text{Total Amount of Drug in Body}}{\text{Plasma Drug Concentration}}$$ A drug with a high $V_d$ indicates that more of the drug is distributed in tissues rather than plasma.

Using the loading dose formula: $$LD = \frac{V_d \times C_{\text{target}}}{F}$$ A drug has $V_d = 30 \text{ L}$, target concentration $C_{\text{target}} = 10 \text{ mg/L}$, and bioavailability $F = 1.0$. What is the loading dose?
A nurse administers Insulin Glargine to a patient. Two hours later, the patient becomes diaphoretic, tremulous, and confused with a blood glucose of 48 mg/dL. What is the priority intervention?

options.text: Administer 15–20 g of fast-acting carbohydrate orally if the patient can swallow safely
Administer another dose of Insulin Glargine to stabilize glucose
Place the patient in Trendelenburg position and monitor

questions.questionText: The _____ route of drug administration has 100% bioavailability because it bypasses first-pass metabolism entirely.
Analyze the opioid analgesic comparison table below. Which drug requires the lowest dose to achieve equianalgesic effect compared to 10 mg of IV Morphine?
A patient with chronic kidney disease (CrCl = 20 mL/min) is prescribed a renally-cleared antibiotic. Compared to a patient with normal renal function, the dose interval should generally be _____.

options.text: Kept the same with no adjustment needed
The drug should always be given IV instead of PO

questions.questionText: Digoxin toxicity is more likely when serum potassium levels are low because hypokalemia increases the binding affinity of Digoxin to $\text{Na}^+/\text{K}^+$-ATPase receptors.

A hospitalized patient is receiving IV Heparin. The aPTT result is 120 seconds (therapeutic range: 60–100 seconds). The patient has no signs of bleeding. Using the weight-based heparin protocol in the table below, what is the correct action?

options.text: Hold heparin for 1 hour, then reduce rate by 20%, recheck aPTT in 6 hours
Increase the heparin infusion rate by 20%
Continue the infusion at the same rate and recheck aPTT in 24 hours

tableData: Increase rate by 25%, recheck in 6 hours
Increase rate by 10%, recheck in 6 hours
Hold 1 hour, reduce rate by 20%, recheck in 6 hours
Hold 2 hours, reduce rate by 30%, notify physician, recheck in 6 hours

questions.questionText: Clearance ($CL$) of a drug is defined as: $$CL = k_e \times V_d$$ where $k_e$ is the elimination rate constant and $V_d$ is the volume of distribution. A drug with $k_e = 0.1 \text{ hr}^{-1}$ and $V_d = 50 \text{ L}$ has a clearance of _____ L/hr.

A 72-year-old woman is brought to the ED confused and bradycardic (HR = 42 bpm). Her medication list includes Metoprolol 100 mg twice daily, Amlodipine 10 mg daily, and Digoxin 0.25 mg daily. Her serum Digoxin level is 3.8 ng/mL (therapeutic: 0.5–2.0 ng/mL). Which of the following is the most appropriate immediate intervention?

options.text: Give an additional dose of Metoprolol to control heart rate
Start a Dopamine infusion at high doses immediately
Administer Atropine 0.5 mg and discharge with close follow-up
